Hi Samira / QuantumEdge team,

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, we want to capture the proposed dedicated capacity layout and next steps so procurement and IR teams have a single reference. High-level items below — I9ve ccrishi, Grace and Dev to handle technical provisioning and the onboarding schedule.

Ask (for this thread): please confirm the regional split (US vs EU), target peak concurrency (rps) and any specific hardware constraints you require (H100 vs A100). Once we have confirmation we9ll publish the implementation plan and a DocuSign-ready statement of work.

Proposed (based on call):
- Primary regions: eu-west1 (low-latency EU customers), us-west2 (West coast US traffic)
- Model config: 2 model variants for production — high-accuracy (FP16, H100 preferred in EU) and cost-optimized (int8/A100 in US)
- GPU pool sizing: staged start with min pool = 4 GPUs across both regions, target steady-state pool = 12 GPUs, burst cap = 24 (preemptible / spot nodes allowed for non-SLA traffic)
- Autoscaling/burst policy: min nodes (keep warm) = 2 per region; policy = queue-based scale-up with immediate burst allowance (up to burst cap) under sustained queue >60s for >2m; automatic cooldown 5m
- Caching: prefix/KV prewarm on rollout; recommend baseline cache warmers for first 48h after deployment
- Network/security: private peering and customer VPC setup; see attached network-reqs.txt for initial checklist

Attachments: draft implementation plan (QE-dedicated-implementation-plan-v1.xlsx), capacity-scaling-proposal.pdf, network-reqs.txt

Next steps:
1) Samira / Jordan confirm regions, H100 requirement, and preferred start week.
2) Redwood to produce final implementation plan + DocuSign SOW.
3) Schedule onboarding kickoff with Infra & CS.

Thanks — I9ll wait for confirmation and will move the SOW to DocuSign after procurement signoff.

Thanks Monica — appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Regions: EU is priority (most of our customers are EU) — primary region should be eu-west1. We will keep a smaller presence in US-west2 for latency-sensitive West Coast accounts, but EU is the SLA region.
2) Hardware: prefer H100 in eu-west1 for our higher-context models (80-100k context), we can accept A100 80GB in US-west2 for the cost-optimized variant. If H100 lead time is long we9re ok with hybrid start (mix H100+A100) as long as we can pin model variants to hardware.
3) Scale targets: target peak concurrency ~220 concurrent streams (chat-like sessions) across both regions. Expected sustained 95th percentile token throughput ~65k tokens/min during peak.
4) SLA expectations: 99.5% runtime for primary EU region; we need fallback policy documented if EU capacity is constrained (automatic failover to US w/ routing + notification).

Procurement: looking to start onboarding the week of 2027-03-21. Procurement will need the SOW and an est. MRR estimate before we sign. Jordan, can you work with Monica on SOW and sign date?

Hi all — quick technical readout and constraints from the infra side. Summarizing options and lead times so procurement has context: 

1) Recommended baseline per-region config (start):
   - eu-west1: 4x H100 (80GB) GPUs in a dedicated pool; software pinned to H100 profiles for high-accuracy variant
   - us-west2: 4x A100 (80GB) GPUs for cost-optimized variant
   - Start pooled nodes so we can support the hot cache and reduce cold-start token cost

2) Autoscale policy (details):
   - min_nodes_per_region = 2 (always warm)
   - target_scale_up = queue-based + request-rate triggers; immediate "burst" allowance = +50% of steady pool up to overall burst cap (candidate: preemptible instances to hit burst cap quickly)
   - cool_down = 5 minutes after last scale event; scale-down incremental (min 1 node per event) to avoid oscillation
   - prewarm behavior: on deployment or rollout we run cache-warmers to populate prefix/KV caches for top N prompts (configurable)

3) Burst considerations and cost control:
   - We can configure a two-tier burst: soft-burst (pre-warmed reserved burst nodes) and hard-burst (ephemeral preemptible). Soft-burst costs more but is covered by SLA-sensitive traffic. Hard-burst is cheaper but not SLA-backed.

4) Lead times and procurement guidance:
   - H100 capacity in eu-west1 currently has a ~3-5 week lead time for guaranteed dedicated capacity (depending on cluster reservations). A hybrid start (mix of H100 + A100) allows you to start earlier while we lock additional H100 capacity.
   - Preemptible/spot quota for burst typically provisioned within 72 hours if we have account limits in place.

5) Network and egress: ensure private peering established ahead of rollout; will need firewall and subnets from QuantumEdge infra team (see network-reqs.txt).

I9ve attached a short PDF (capacity-scaling-proposal.pdf) that maps these policies to likely cost bands. Happy to sync on a short call to walk through numbers.

- Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jordan / Samira — thanks for the questions. Consolidating answers and next steps below (SOW + cost est will follow this afternoon):

1) MRR estimate: we9re preparing a short cost appendix that shows three bands (baseline, baseline+soft-burst, baseline+soft+hard-burst). The baseline (start size above) is estimated at ~$62,000/month. Soft-burst adds approximately $18k/month (reserved burst nodes to meet SLA), and hard-burst (preemptible) usage is billed on consumption and typically ~ $4k-$9k/month during high season. We9ll include a sensitivity table in the SOW.

2) SLA / hybrid start language: draft SOW will call out primary SLA for eu-west1 (99.5%). For hybrid start we9ll include an explicit fallback policy: automatic routing to us-west2 when eu capacity is unavailable, with notification to QuantumEdge engineers and a remediation timeline (attempt remediation within 30m, escalate to on-call if unresolved at 60m). Soft-burst nodes are SLA-backed; hard-burst (preemptible) is marked as non-SLA and for best-effort overflow.

3) Timing: H100 final capacity guarantee is 3-5 weeks. Given QuantumEdge target week of 2027-03-21 we9re likely to need a hybrid start. We can ship an SOW and kickoff for 3/22 and begin provisioning the hybrid pool. H100 fulfillment target: early April (we will update procurement with firm dates after reservation).

Attachments: QE-dedicated-implementation-plan-v1.xlsx (SOW draft + implementation checklist).
